Innovative Training in Neuroscience
The Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program (INP) oversees the graduate program and serves as the hub for neuroscience research at the University of Texas at Austin. With over 90 diverse faculty advancing knowledge in areas ranging from molecular neuroscience and genetics to physiology, cellular and systems neuroscience, cognition and behavior, and the neurobiology of disease, the INP provides a collaborative, cutting-edge environment for training and discovery.
Apply
Director’s Welcome
Welcome to the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program (INP) at UT Austin! Our program fosters an environment where creativity and innovation thrive, fueled by collaboration and a passion for discovery. Research in the INP spans the full spectrum of neuroscience disciplines and methodologies. As an INP student, you’ll break down traditional academic boundaries and develop the skills, knowledge, and experience to pursue a range of career paths. The journey of discovery is rarely linear, but with curiosity and perseverance, it can be profoundly rewarding, and we’ll support you every step of the way. I invite you to explore our program, connect with our community, and envision how you can help shape the future of neuroscience at UT Austin.
Jarrod Lewis-Peacock
Director, Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program
About the Program
Research and training at the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program (INP) is diverse with investigators covering all major disciplines and techniques in neuroscience and representing multiple domains of scientific inquiry. Because of the outstanding and diverse composition of the INP faculty, our graduate students are provided with unparalleled opportunities for research and are trained to become critical thinkers capable of understanding the full breadth of conceptual and technical approaches to neuroscience.
